newsitem.title: NORWAY: Analysts downgrade EPS estimates for Hydro.
newsitem.headline: Analysts downgrade EPS estimates for Hydro.

text.p: Three out of four analysts Reuters spoke to on Monday said they intended to downgrade estimates for 1997 earnings per share (EPS) for Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA.
The fourth analyst said he would hold his already-low estimate at 30.3 crowns per share.

Shares in Norway's largest listed company fell heavily on Monday after the group announced a 10 percent decline in 1996 operating profit to 9.65 billion crowns, attributing it to lower earnings from metals and petrochemicals.
The result fell more than one billion crowns below market expectations.

"It is clearly not good. There are certain special circumstances in the figures, but overall these special factors even out and the figures reflect the true underlying growth in revenues," said one analyst, who said he would adjust his 1997 EPS estimate downwards after consideration.
Another analyst, explaining why Hydro's result fell so far short of expectations, said: "The main problem lies in light metals and agriculture. That's where everything went wrong."
Most of the analysts said they had been over-optimistic on earnings at Hydro's aluminium division.

"Hydro says there is a lag of four to six months before a rise in aluminium prices will be reflected in its results. But there has been a tendency among analysts to already include higher prices," said another.
A Reuter poll of 10 analysts before the results forecast EPS for 1997 at 32.3 crowns. All four of today's analysts were included in that poll.
The analysts said they expected Hydro's share price to head lower on Tuesday once foreign investors had digested the figures.
AT 1455 GMT, Hydro stood 30.5 crowns down at 348 crowns, a fall of eight percent.
